summary: ZenithPrime multiplexed-stream reassembly failure after regional failover causing truncated conversation state
description: Issue summary: During a partial regional failover in us-east (2026-03-12 11:43 UTC -> 12:10 UTC), ZenithPrime observed truncated chat transcripts and loss of ordered response segments for long-lived multiplexed WebSocket sessions. Impact: Several customer connections experienced missing completion fragments and session-level state mismatch. Estimated affected traffic: ~2.1% of ZenithPrime production traffic (peak QPS window). Environment: prod-us-east, multiplexed streaming over WebSocket via api-gateway.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Establish a multiplexed WebSocket session using multiplex ID header (x-rw-multiplex-id). 2) Simulate long-lived stream with intermittent micro-failures (short connection resets). 3) Trigger a control-plane region failover or simulate egress path change that rebinds to a different gateway instance. 4) Observe fragment reassembly: client sees truncated last segment or receives segments out-of-order when session resumes.
logs: Relevant logs found in api-gateway and multiplexer; sample correlation id: z-prime-20260312-11:46:22-cid-9f3a. Gateway error: 'mux: missing fragment: stream_id=0x7f2a'. Multiplexer trace: reassembly attempted with stale stream-sequence (seq=472 -> 1) after connection bind. Serving-runtime side shows matched requests but missing final token chunks at the router layer. Packet capture indicates connection reused a previously retired stream identifier during reconnection.
investigation_notes: Timeline: 11:40 UTC - traffic spike + control-plane config push; 11:43 UTC - partial failover triggered by planned routing change; 11:44-11:58 UTC - customers report truncated transcripts; 12:04 UTC - mitigations applied; 12:10 UTC - global fallback to alternate multiplexer behavior; 12:18 UTC - full resolution.
hypothesis: The multiplexer connection-reuse logic contained a race where a recycled connection could reuse a numeric stream id without clearing per-connection reassembly state. During a failover the API gateway reattached the same multiplex id to a new upstream connection but left reassembly buffers that referenced the old sequence numbers, causing the reassembly engine to drop subsequent fragments or treat them as out-of-order.
mitigation: 1) Immediate: deployed emergency proxy rule to force new multiplexed sessions to use globally unique session tokens (session hash appended) instead of numeric ids; 2) Fallback: enabled conservative reassembly mode (strict-seq-check) to drop ambiguous fragments rather than interleave; 3) Customer-level workaround: asked affected customers to restart active multiplexed sessions during the window.
root_cause: A race in streaming-multiplexer connection recycling that failed to zero per-connection fragment state combined with control-plane failover that reassigned multiplex ids. Edge case only triggered under long-lived sessions that experienced connection handoff across gateway processes.
resolution: Patch merged (PR #4821) to always tombstone stream ids on connection shutdown and to attach a session-unique nonce to multiplex ids. Hotfix rolled to prod-us-east at 2026-03-12T12:04:00Z; full rollout to other regions completed by 2026-03-13. Added unit and integration tests for reconnection/reassembly scenarios. Backfill: reprocessed telemetry to detect other customers with similar traces and contacted them directly.
post_incident_actions: 1) Add explicit reassembly-state-clearing to runbook and orchestration hooks. 2) Instrument new metric: mux.reassembly.conflicts and alert at >5/m. 3) Schedule a capacity test for long-lived multiplexed sessions under failover next quarter. 4) Update API docs with recommended session restart guidance. 5) Offer ZenithPrime a service credit and dedicated follow-up call to review mitigations.
